text:
incident-bot: ALERT: High CPU usage + OOMs on deployment/token-preproc in cluster/us-east-1a. 23 pods reporting OOMKilled in the last 5m. Error signature looks like repeated tokenization loops -> CPU saturation. @sam (oncall) paged. :rotating_light:
sam (oncall): acked. I'm taking this. any customer-facing impact yet?
maya (sre): seeing 5xx spike on /v1/generate and increased tail latency on embeddings requests. Some requests get 502 from envoy when backend pods die.
tara (support): two customers reported degraded responses and timeouts starting ~10:12am. No P0 yet but impacting a handful of mid-tier tenants.
jin (infra): nodes in us-east-1a show high system load on preproc nodes and a couple are hitting kubelet OOM kills for containers. I see one node with repeated docker/containerd errors around the same time.
alex (eng-ml): quick note: we rolled token-splitter v2.1 last week. There was a regex fallback path added for edge-case scripts that might be quadratic on certain long prompts. Could be related.
sam (oncall): plan: 1) drain a couple noisy pods to prevent node-level fallout 2) scale down token-preproc concurrency 3) apply temporary ingress rate limit 4) restart deployment to get pods on healthy nodes. Doing 1->3 now.
ops-bot: runbook step triggered: INCIDENT_TOKEN_PREPROC_HIGH_CPU. Owner: sam (oncall).

sam (oncall): kubectl commands I ran:```bash
# cordon noisy node
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-45-12.us-east-1a
# evict specific preproc pods
kubectl delete pod token-preproc-7f9d8 -n inference
# reduce concurrency via configmap
kubectl set env deployment/token-preproc MAX_WORKERS=4 -n inference
# apply temporary ingress rate limit
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: temp-rate-limit
spec:
  # simplified for incident
EOF
```

maya (sre): after scaling MAX_WORKERS down to 4 CPU usage dropped ~30% on the remaining pods. But we still see occasional OOMKilled events when a particularly long prompt comes through.

jin (infra): I identified one node with GPU drivers reporting CUDA errors earlier but that was on a different node pool (gpu-pool). No evidence the GPU issue caused preproc OOMs, but I'll mark the node for audit.

alex (eng-ml): can we add a timeout/truncation in the pre-tokenizer path? If certain clients send enormous single-line prompts with thousands of tokens, the fallback regex blows up. Suggest fast patch: cap input length pre-tokenize to 8k chars and reject with 413.

sam (oncall): temporary mitigation: adding a fast-length-check in front of token-splitter deploy via config flag. Rolling that out now as config change so we can roll back if needed.

maya (sre): logs from a killed pod:```json
{"level":"error","msg":"worker panic: runtime: out of memory","pod":"token-preproc-9bcd2","reason":"OOMKilled","stack":"goroutine 42 [running]: ..."}
```

tara (support): updating affected customers: message sent to two customers with ETA ~30m for stabilization. Asked to collect any payloads/examples they can share.

sam (oncall): after the config change and reduced concurrency we see stabilized CPU on the fleet, 95th latency for tokenization is back to normal for most traffic. A small subset of requests still cause pod restarts; I'm rate-limiting at the ingress at 20rps per client to protect the pool.

ops-bot: FLAG: create issue INF-5123 for root-cause analysis and a postmortem.

alex (eng-ml): created patch PR to add upfront length cap + fast-path sanitizer in token-splitter. Also adding a unit test for pathological input. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/rep/token-splitter/pull/248

jin (infra): note: we also increased kubelet eviction threshold temporarily to reduce churning while we stabilize, will revert post-incident.

maya (sre): customer impact summary: ~6 tenants experienced increased errors/timeouts between 10:12-10:42am; after mitigations we saw recovery and no persistent data loss. Flagging for Severity 3.

sam (oncall): handing off to night oncall @maya in 30m. I'll leave the rate-limiter, MAX_WORKERS=4, and the config length-cap in place. Next steps for follow-up: - roll out token-splitter hotfix to prod (alex) - add telemetry for fallbacks/regex-path (eng-ml) - add alert for token-preproc CPU burn pattern - run a soak test for long-prompt cases

maya (sre): acked handoff. I'll monitor for the next 2 hours and coordinate with infra to revert kubelet thresholds once stable. Will open postmortem and link to INF-5123.

sam (oncall): thanks all. closing page for now but keeping incident channel open for updates. :white_check_mark:
